title: The Bosphorus Brief — 15 September 2026
overview: The dominant story today is a wide-scale crackdown on LGBTQ+ groups and HIV support organizations across Turkey, drawing sharp EU concern and split domestic coverage. Beyond that, a migrant boat tragedy near Greece and steady economic data round out a day light on immediate resident-facing paperwork news, though rights and mobility remain the throughline.

sections.heading: LGBTQ+ Crackdown Draws EU Concern
sections.body: Turkish authorities have arrested dozens linked to LGBTQ+ and HIV support groups, raided rights organizations' offices, and blocked associated websites and social accounts, according to AP, i24NEWS, and GO Magazine. The EU said it is 'concerned,' and an EU rapporteur on Turkey described the operations as pulling the country down 'a dark path' (Bianet). Coverage diverges by lens: state media (Al Jazeera, Anadolu-adjacent framing) has reported the raids with minimal comment, while opposition-leaning and international outlets (Turkish Minute, France24, AP) emphasize the scale of arrests and the pressure on civil society groups. For foreign residents connected to affected organizations, colleagues, or programs, this is worth monitoring closely, including any downstream effects on NGO registrations or partner visas.

sections.heading: Migrant Boat Tragedy Near Greece
sections.body: At least one person died and 25 remain missing after a migrant boat sank near a Greek island, reported by Anadolu, Euronews, and InfoMigrants. This adds to a difficult year for Aegean crossings and is a reminder for anyone with family or contacts attempting sea routes that conditions remain dangerous as autumn weather sets in.

sections.heading: Money and Rates
sections.body: The Turkish Central Bank held its policy rate steady at 37% for a fifth straight meeting, with markets now expecting an October cut (BiggO, Turkish Minute). Lira deposit rates have meanwhile slipped to their lowest since 2023 (Hürriyet Daily News), a signal worth watching for anyone holding TRY savings. The exchange rate sits at USD/TRY 48.61, EUR/TRY 56.38 — a further note of the lira's gradual depreciation this year. Separately, Turkey reported USD 13.1 billion in foreign direct investment amid shifting global portfolio strategies.

sections.heading: Regional Safety Notes
sections.body: Houthi forces attacked Saudi Arabia as Gulf-Iran talks were postponed, and a pipeline attack could affect global oil supply, though US energy officials expect resumption soon (Middle East Eye, Japan Times). None of this directly affects Turkey travel, but it's part of a tense regional backdrop. No new M4+ earthquakes were recorded near Turkey since early September; the most recent was a M4.1 near Sulakyurt on September 3. Travel advisory levels remain unchanged: Türkiye at L2, with neighboring Syria, Iraq, Iran, and Lebanon all at L4.

closing: Stay steady, keep an eye on the LGBTQ+ rights story as it develops, and have a good Tuesday.
